messages.subject: SNP markers with recombination fraction higher than 0.5
messages.subject_clean: SNP markers with recombination fraction higher than 0.5
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,
I am trying to create a linkage map with data from allotetraploid crop. I have 90 individuals and ~2.5 K SNPs after the QC applied following the KW. Broman manual.

Based on the graph of LOD scores vs rf (gotten with the code below)I can see there are many pairs of markers with rf > 1/2 (0.5 to ~0.8). The LOD scores for those pair of markers are lower than 5.

plot(as.numeric(rf), as.numeric(lod), xlab = "Recombination fraction", ylab = "LOD score"

I have tried to identify those strange markers with the function checkAlleles but the output says is "No apparent problems".

In addition by plotting the estimates of rf (gotten with the code below) I can see there is only one linkage group instead of 26.

lg <- formLinkageGroups(goshir, max.rf = 0.35, min.lod = 6)
plotRF(goshir, alternate.chrid = TRUE)

Any feedback or idea about this issue in my data will be greatly appreciate it.

Fers

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] SNP markers with recombination fraction higher than 0.5
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] SNP markers with recombination fraction higher than 0.5
messages.body_plain:
R/qtl is exclusively for diploid organisms, so with an allotetraploid you maybe need to look elsewhere?

what sort of cross?

Estimated rf > 1/2 is fine for pairs that aren’t actually linked. I mean, if the true recombination fraction is 1/2, then the estimate will be 1/2 +/- something, and the LOD score should be small.

In formLinkageGroups, you want to vary max.rf and min.lod to get more than 1 group.

I’d also look at the segregation of the markers with geno.table(). If things aren’t segregating 1:1 or 1:2:1 you can get inappropriate evidence for linkage.

karl

messages.subject: Cross type for DH population
messages.body_plain:
Hello Karl,

I have a question regarding Bi-parental QTL mapping. In my genotype data, three parents are involved, e.g., X, Y, Z. All my materials are inbred lines and double-haploids. So, the individuals I have are either X*Y or X*Z. My genotype data is A, B, H translated. So, A= Homozygous for parent A(AA), B= Homozygous for parent B(BB), H=Heterozygous(AB).X was always considered to be as parent A and Y/Z was considered as parent B while doing the ABH translation.

I am confused, which cross type should I use in RQtl? If I use “cross-type =DH” it shows warning messages as three genotypes are involved. Should I replace all H with missing values so that R can read it as DH or is it ok if I use “F2” as cross-type(which comes by default in “read. cross” function if I don´t specify the cross type?

Thank you very much. Any suggestion would be highly appreciated.

Regards

Ishrat

messages.body_plain:
As I understand it, you have two different crosses, X x Y and X x Z, but that you’re pooling them. But what sort of crosses were they? If they are doubled haploid populations, there shouldn’t be any H genotypes at all. Whether to use “dh” or “f2” depends on the nature of the cross that produced the individuals you’re considering.

karl

messages.subject: Best strategy to construct high density genetic map when phsical positions are avilable for only subset of total markers.
messages.subject_clean: Best strategy to construct high density genetic map when phsical positions are avilable for only subset of total markers.
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,
I am working with rice (diploid) RIL population and I am trying to construct high density genetic map with ~14000 SNPs. I have following queries

1)Of the total 14000 SNPs I have physical positions for ~10000 SNPs but dont have the physical positions for remaining 4000 SNPs. I want to use these 14000 markers together so as to identify genetic positions of 4000 SNPs (with unknown physical positions) realtive to  10000 SNPs (with known physical positions). What will be the best strategy to accomplish my goal. Is there any way I can use available physical positions with est.map function?

2) When I am trying to estimate RF many of my markers are showing RF > 0.5 (with high LOD) even though none of these markers switched (I have already eliminated distorted as well as duplicated markers) and therefore SNPs belonging physically to same chromosomes are getting split in to multiple LGs.  What could be the possible cause behind this and how I should proceed with this.

I will appreciate any suggestions in this regard.

messages.subject: Re: Cross type for DH population
messages.body_plain:
Hello Karl,
Thanks for your kind reply. Actually, I am using secondary data from a commercial pre-breeding program. It is not unusual for commercial pre-breeding to have some level of heterozygosity in the DH lines (which my populations were) due to the methodology of production and growing those DH lines. In practice, unless every spike (which was not done) is bagged the high amount of sterility allows for outcrossing and therefore the chance of heterozygosity is increased. That´s why I got very few H also in my genotype data. I have decided to consider all "H" as missing values and then to use cross-type as "DH".And I have asked for the information regarding the nature of the cross that produced the individuals but haven´t got any reply yet.

Thank you. I hope I am on the right track and any kind of suggestion would be valuable for me.

Regards
Ishrat
